items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We spent a few days in my brother's home and one day we decided to visit my Uncle Ernest Coleman

ctx.x: My brother, his wife, an uncle and cousin John Coleman also lived on the hill and not too far from my father. We gave a party, my brother gave one and many of his or his wife's friends gave parties and that's the way our visit to Cincinnati was spent most of the time. My old boss Clarence Page also invited us to his house as did my good friend from way back, William Smith, who was known as "Smittie" and who had changed his name to Smyth. He was a union delegate and still playing piano in clubs. Clarence Page waa…

We spent a few days in my brother's home and one day we decided to visit my Uncle Ernest Coleman, who did not live far from my brother. As we were a mixed married couple, trouble could be around any corner and it was around one this day. We were not far from my brother's place when it started to rain but not hard. One of my brother's step daughters was with us and we sent her back to the house to get an umbrella.

Lily was carrying a very light coloured handbag and did not want to get it wet. I had on a raincoat so she gave the handbag to me and I put it under my raincoat and held it with one hand. Just as Lily gave me the handbag, a police patrol car was passing and one of the two police saw the action. They stopped the car and one of them jumped out and came beside me. He said: Give me that purse, I saw you snatch it. I said: this is my wife (speaking about Lily) and further more, if I had snatched the bag, do you think…
